main.title: Kingdom Hearts III
main.summary: Kingdom Hearts III is a 2019 action role-playing game developed and published by Square Enix.

cards.heading: The Dark Seeker Saga reaches its conclusion
cards.text: Kingdom Hearts III is a 2019 action role-playing game developed and published by Square Enix. It is the third main installment in the Kingdom Hearts series and the twelfth game overall, and serves as a conclusion of the "Dark Seeker Saga" story arc that began with the original game. Set after the events of Kingdom Hearts 3D: Dream Drop Distance, returning protagonist Sora is joined by Donald Duck, Goofy, King Mickey, and Riku in their search for seven guardians of light as they attempt to thwart Xehanort's plan to bring about a second Keyblade War. Their journey has them cross paths with characters and visit worlds based on different Disney intellectual properties, also being the first game in the series to include content based on Pixar productions.

cards.heading: An adventure across Disney and Pixar worlds
cards.text: Concepts for Kingdom Hearts III began as early as 2005 after the release of Kingdom Hearts II in Japan, with the game's development not being officially announced until 2013, following years of rumors and speculation. The game features recurring gameplay elements from the series, while expanding parties to five characters total, introducing new "Attraction Flow" attacks that incorporate various Disney Parks attractions, and including minigames inspired by classic Mickey Mouse cartoons in the style of 1980s LCD games.

cards.heading: Release, reception and later editions
cards.text: Kingdom Hearts III reached PlayStation 4 and Xbox One in January 2019. Reviews praised its visual style, music and range of combat options, while the presentation of its story drew a more divided response. More than five million copies shipped, including downloads, during the first week. The Re Mind expansion followed in 2020, extending the adventure, and later editions combined it with the main game. That continuing release history brought the conclusion to other platforms, but its initial appeal lay in giving familiar characters and worlds a much larger space for movement and combat.
